Bootstrap classification confidence for one group

Source: R/bootstrapConfidence.R
bootstrapClassify.Rd

The single-group worker behind bootstrapLineageConfidence(). Trains a classifier on one group's cells, then repeatedly resamples each cell's counts (multinomial resampling) and re-predicts its class. The fraction of resamples assigning a cell to each class is its confidence for that class.

Usage

bootstrapClassify(
  countMat,
  labels,
  nBoot = 100,
  nPerClass = 50,
  cores = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  classifier = c("pcaLogistic", "logistic", "rf", "lda", "svm"),
  ntree = 500,
  priors = c("balanced", "observed"),
  correctedCounts = FALSE
)

Arguments

countMat

A cells x genes matrix of raw (non-negative integer) counts for the cells of one group. Normalised or log-transformed values are rejected, since the resampling needs each cell's total transcript count.

labels

Character vector of the original cell type label for each row of countMat.

nBoot

Number of bootstrap resamples.

nPerClass

Minimum number of training cells per class; classes smaller than this are up-sampled with replacement.

cores

Number of cores to run the bootstrap resamples on (forked with BiocParallel); the default runs serially. On Windows, where forking is not available, it always runs serially. If seed is given, the results are identical whatever the number of cores.

seed

Random seed for reproducibility, or NULL. Recommended for reproducibility.

classifier

One of "pcaLogistic" (ridge multinomial logistic regression, via glmnet, with the penalty chosen by cross-validation, on the first 50 principal components of the training cells, computed exactly for up to 5,000 genes and with irlba beyond; the default), "logistic" (the same on all genes), "rf" (random forest, via randomForest), "lda" (linear discriminant analysis, via MASS) or "svm" (support vector machine, via e1071).

ntree

Number of trees; only used when classifier = "rf".

priors

The classifier is trained with balanced classes, which gives every class the same prior. "balanced" keeps those equal priors; "observed" weights each class by its share of the cells, so a resample is assigned to its most probable class given how common the classes are.

correctedCounts

FALSE (the default) requires whole-number counts. TRUE also accepts counts that are not whole numbers, such as counts corrected for ambient RNA, and resamples them as they are. They must still be on the scale of molecule counts: a cell's resample draws as many transcripts as its total (rounded), so normalised or log-transformed values would give the wrong amount of resampling noise.

Value

A numeric matrix with one row per cell (in the order of countMat) and one column per class in labels. Entry [i, k] is the fraction of bootstrap resamples in which cell i was classified as class k, so each row sums to 1.

Examples

data(lungSubset)
endo = lungSubset$cellType %in% c("Arteriole", "Venous", "Capillary", "Lymphatic")
#> Loading required namespace: SpatialExperiment
countMat = t(as.matrix(SummarizedExperiment::assay(lungSubset, "counts")[, endo]))
freq = bootstrapClassify(countMat, lungSubset$cellType[endo], nBoot = 5, seed = 1)
#> Minimum class size: 108
#> Finished training classifier.
head(freq)
#>      Capillary Venous Lymphatic Arteriole
#> [1,]       0.4    0.0       0.6         0
#> [2,]       1.0    0.0       0.0         0
#> [3,]       1.0    0.0       0.0         0
#> [4,]       1.0    0.0       0.0         0
#> [5,]       1.0    0.0       0.0         0
#> [6,]       0.8    0.2       0.0         0
